label: MARRIAGE REPAIR

cover.headline: Rebuilding trust after *small broken promises*
cover.sub: 5 ways to make your word count again.

points.heading: Small things add up
points.body: Forgetting to call, missing a pickup. Each one alone is minor. Together, they wear trust down.
points.panel: Notice which small promises matter most to each of you.

points.heading: Promise less, keep more
points.body: Saying “I’ll try” honestly is better than a confident yes you can’t keep.
points.panel: “I’m not sure I can, but I’ll let you know by noon.”

points.heading: Name it when you slip
points.body: Owning a missed promise quickly keeps it from becoming a pattern.
points.panel: “I said I’d call and I didn’t. I’m sorry.”

points.heading: Ask for what you need clearly
points.body: If his slips hurt, say so calmly, without a list of every past one.
points.panel: “When plans change last minute, I feel forgotten. Can you text me?”

points.heading: Notice when promises are kept
points.body: Rebuilding trust is easier when progress is seen.

close.save: Save this for a fresh start.

caption:
Trust usually isn’t broken by one big moment. More often, it’s worn down by small promises that slip through the cracks.

The good news is that it can be rebuilt the same way: one small, kept promise at a time.

Save this, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
